title: Feasts are not consecrated to angels or Saints, though a solemn commemoration, as in the English liturgy, is allowed
source_text: XXVI. Eodem modo negant licitum esse dies festos Angelis, & hominibus Beatis consecrare, cum festa ad cultum Dei solemnem pertineant, quamvis nihil obstare putent quin certis diebus Sanctorum quorundam fiat peculiaris & solemnis commemoratio, & gratiae Deo agantur pro beneficiis in ipsos, & per ipsos collatis, eorumque virtutes ac egregia facta populo Christiano imitanda proponantur. Nam ejusmodi festa Deo soli consecrata sunt, quanquam in magnum Sanctorum virorum honorem cedant, ut in Ecclesia Anglicana obtinet, in cujus Liturgia memorantur Apostolorum, & quorundam aliorum virorum Sanctorum festa.
pass_a_gloss: In the same way they deny that it is lawful to consecrate feast days to angels and blessed men, since feasts belong to the solemn cult of God, although they think nothing prevents a peculiar and solemn commemoration of certain Saints being made on certain days, and thanks being given to God for benefits conferred on them and through them, and their virtues and excellent deeds being set before the Christian people to be imitated. For feasts of that sort are consecrated to God alone, although they redound to the great honor of holy men, as holds in the English Church, in whose liturgy the feasts of the Apostles and of certain other holy men are remembered.
pass_b_english: Feast days may not be consecrated to angels or the blessed, because feasts belong to God's solemn worship.
A set day may still solemnly remember certain Saints, thank God for benefits given to them and through them, and propose their virtues for imitation.
Such days are consecrated to God alone, even while they honor holy men.
The English liturgy, which remembers apostles and other holy men, is the example.

choices.why: Distinguishes a memorial day from a feast consecrated to the Saint.
